newsitem.title: GERMANY: No obstacles seen to more German DAX gains.
newsitem.headline: No obstacles seen to more German DAX gains.

text.p: German shares shot higher yet again on Wednesday, powering to fresh records amid a whole range of positive market factors, and dealers said they saw no signs that the market would break its uptrend.
"There seems to be nothing around to brake us at the moment," said a Frankfurt trader.
"The dollar is giving us a push, Bunds are helping, the U.S. is helping and there are no negative corporate stories out there. I don't see any justification for pulling out, even at these highs."
The IBIS DAX was up 31.93 points at 4,062.03 at 0823 GMT.
September DTB DAX futures were up 35 points at 4,085 points.

Several research houses were targeting 4,100 points on the DAX today but some traders were sceptical. Some were caught wrongfooted by the continued rise in the DAX over the 4,000 point level, which many had seen as a natural peak.
"I could see maybe 10 or 20 more points in it. We have done quite a lot already," one trader said.
Shares were higher across the board.
Retailer Metro, already in favour after saying it might buy a Dutch cash and carry firm, posted further gains.
The company, whose shareholder meeting takes place today, said it expected its operating profit this year to exceed the 1.06 billion marks it achieved in 1996.
Dealers said analysts at several German research houses had recommended the stock.
